title: DFS Bound for Masked Mutual Information
summary: The DFS bound estimating masked d-tuple leakage from single-share information remains conjectural; proving it without the square-root loss from statistical distance is open.

formal_statement.body: Prove the DFS bound on masked mutual information without the square-root loss from reduction to statistical distance.

scope.domain: Side-channel cryptanalysis of masked implementations through mutual-information leakage bounds.
assumptions: Independent Shares' Leakage (ISL) assumption for reducing d-share leakage to single-share leakage.
parameters: d: number of share leakages in the masked tuple
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove the conjectured DFS mutual-information bound without the square-root loss introduced by reduction to statistical distance.

citations.label: Masking Proofs Are Tight and How to Exploit it in Security Evaluations

progress.summary: The source presents the DFS bound as only conjectured and identifies an ignored square-root loss in the reduction from mutual information to statistical distance used in the proofs.
citation_labels: Vincent Grosso et al., Masking Proofs Are Tight and How to Exploit it in Security Evaluations
